articles.title: Psychology says people who hate having their mistakes pointed out may be protecting their self-esteem, not just their ego
articles.description: People who dislike having their mistakes pointed out are often reacting to more than the correction itself. Their response may be influenced by factors such as self-esteem, cognitive dissonance, emotional regulation, mindset, and past experiences with criticism. At the same time, this doesn't mean every defensive reaction is appropriate or that constructive feedback should be avoided. Instead, it highlights how personal history and emotions can shape the way people receive criticism.

articles.description: Rahul Gandhi accused Home Minister Amit Shah of police brutality against NEET protesters. He stated he was not allowed to speak in Lok Sabha and refused to apologize. Gandhi claimed students were beaten with pellet guns and lathis with nails. Delhi Police issued a fact check rejecting claims of gunshot injuries. The opposition has repeatedly raised the NEET paper leak issue in Parliament.

articles.title: Russia turns S‐400 into ballistic strike weapon: RM‐48U missiles hammer Patriot-less Ukraine?
articles.description: Russia is repurposing S‐300/S‐400 interceptors into RM‐48U ground‐attack “zombie missiles,” firing them from air‐defence launchers at Kyiv’s industrial sites while Ukraine tries to stretch scarce Patriot batteries. This segment explains how the modified missiles work, why they’re hitting big plants like Meridian, and how they layer with Iskander, Bastion and North Korean rounds to overwhelm Ukraine’s air shield.

articles.title: Who Is V Kamakoti? IIT Madras Director And Exam Reforms Task Force Member Draws Political Fire
articles.description: IIT Madras Director V. Kamakoti has found himself at the centre of a political controversy after Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi referred to him as a "gaumutra expert" during a Lok Sabha debate. Kamakoti is a Padma Shri awardee, leads the team behind India's indigenous Shakti microprocessor, and has been appointed to the Centre's high-powered task force on examination reforms. Here's a closer look at his academic achievements, national roles, the controversy over his past remarks on gomutra, and his views on preventing paper leaks.

articles.title: 'He Put Pellets Into Blood of Our Students': Rahul Gandhi's Explosive Attack on Amit Shah Sparks Lok Sabha Uproar

articles.title: 'Home minister ordered students to be shot’: Rahul Gandhi’s charge in Lok Sabha
articles.description: Raising the issue during a discussion in the Lok Sabha on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, Gandhi alleged that the Home Minister was absent because he was "scared" and accused him of authorising the firing on students during the protests

articles.title: Kangana Ranaut, CJP's Saurav Das spar over actor's comments on Gen Z protesters
articles.description: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut and CJP spokesperson Saurav Das traded sharp barbs. Ranaut called Gen Z "Generation gutter" and questioned their upbringing. Das criticized Ranaut's language and questioned her mental stability. Ranaut dismissed Das as useless and unemployed, highlighting her career achievements. The exchange occurred amid protests over NEET examination irregularities.

articles.title: Shorts protest at Delhi's St Stephen's: Dress code or personal freedom?
articles.description: A St Stephen's College shorts ban ignites a debate on student freedom and institutional rules. Students protest the new dress code, which restricts attire in classrooms and other college spaces. This controversy highlights a broader trend of disputes over personal appearance on Indian campuses. Colleges face challenges balancing tradition with students' growing expectations of personal autonomy. The situation tests how Indian campuses manage institutional identity and individual liberty.

articles.title: Sagittarius Monthly Nadi Horoscope (August 2026): Nag Panchami Could Expose What Is Damaging a Close Bond
articles.description: August 2026 presents a serious month for Sagittarians concerning shared finances and personal trust. Careful approaches will protect peace and resources during this period. articles.title: Yemen's Houthis considering fees for ships sailing through Red Sea, sources say
articles.description: Yemen's Houthi faction is exploring the potential of levying fees on maritime traffic in the southern Red Sea. This fee proposal emerged from discussions between Iranian officials and Houthi delegates. Interestingly, Chinese vessels are set to be exempt from these charges. Should this plan proceed, it threatens to disturb essential energy shipments and impact international trade, augmenting the existing naval blockade declared by the Houthis against Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Opposition Slams Govt Over Exam Bill, Police Action on Students
articles.description: Congress MP K Suresh criticizes the government's exam amendment bill and police action on protesters. He questions accountability for NTA failures, while Karti Chidambaram calls the bill 'pointless' and says it won't prevent future paper leaks.

articles.title: Iran rules out Oman's proposal for regional joint management of Hormuz Strait, senior Iranian official tells Reuters
articles.description: Iran has rejected Oman's proposal for joint management of the Strait of Hormuz. A senior Iranian official stated the plan has no chance of success. The official added that the US and Saudi Arabia are pressuring Oman. They are trying to advance their unrealistic plans for the strategic waterway. Tehran believes these plans are not feasible for regional cooperation.

articles.title: Bhopal: Farmers block highway, demand MSP for moong, scrap e-token

articles.title: Iraq ‘Exposes’ Ukraine-Linked ‘Militant Cells’ In Secret Intel Operation, Kyiv Denies Claims
articles.description: Iraq has accused alleged militant cells linked to Ukraine of carrying out attacks inside the country, escalating tensions amid growing regional security concerns. Iraqi National Security Adviser Qasim al-Aboudi claimed several suspects confessed to working for Ukraine, an allegation Kyiv has strongly denied as "unfounded and unsubstantiated." The claims come amid renewed accusations over drone attacks in the region, while Russia has echoed Iraq's allegations. Watch the full report for the latest developments and reactions from Baghdad, Kyiv, and Moscow.

articles.title: "Whatever I give her, it will never equal what she gave me": How Lamine Yamal refused to blame his mother despite childhood struggles that changed his life forever
articles.description: Lamine Yamal, the 19-year-old World Cup winner, has spoken openly about a childhood shaped by financial hardship and parental sacrifice. His mother, Sheila Ebana, emigrated from Equatorial Guinea to Spain as a teenager, had Yamal at 16, and raised him largely alone after separating from his father when Lamine was three. Yamal credits her with shielding him from the worst of their circumstances, saying she made him see only the beautiful side of life. He also reflected on his rapid rise at Barcelona, describing himself as a creative and entertaining player who never anticipated reaching the first team quite so quickly

articles.title: Trump: Meet with Zelenskiy, Netanyahu 'positive'
articles.description: Donald Trump described his meetings with leaders as positive. He spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Both leaders were in Washington for a memorial service. Important subjects were discussed during these separate meetings. The discussions reportedly went very well for all involved.

articles.title: India slams POK elections, Pakistan's claims over Indus Valley legacy
articles.description: India has condemned Pakistan's legislative assembly elections in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. The Ministry of External Affairs called the polls a cosmetic exercise to hide illegal occupation. India reiterated its firm stance that the entire Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of India. The spokesperson highlighted Pakistan's promotion of terrorism and religious fundamentalism. This stance questions Pakistan's claims to any pluralistic cultural legacy.
